qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r2/raw-evidence-index.json; qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/tests/functional.cjs lines 185-188 (golden replay of the wall request); server.js sha256 03b52651... matches index
evidence:
Built the criterion->requirement map for all 2 gate, 16 functional, 5 polish and 4 visual criteria. Nearly every leg traces to a public sentence: client scope and plain not-available (walls-and-retention.md:15-17), wall every route incl. transcript address and links/mentions (17), live wall within seconds and only Harriet adds/lifts (19), nested replies >=3 levels with quote and ordering (conversations.md:5), edits/versions/stale edit keeping typed text (9), safe formatting everywhere incl. quote/snippet/versions/transcript and typed 'On hold' (13), message-link preview/not-available (17), mentions (21), unread per user/tabs/new-messages line/mark unread/deleted not counted (25), idempotent resend and stable order in thread/search/transcript (29), live updates preserving draft/scroll/open reply (31), 390 px (33), timer exact-boundary/shorten/off/partner-only (walls-and-retention.md:23), deletion placeholder (25), hold scope/release/held undeletable (29), search case/versions/click-to-message and transcript heading/no controls/held versions (33-35), refusal reason in place (37), restart persistence and no reimport (integration.md:5). Sign-in is house convention (SKILL.md:63; internal annotation row 28) and is also explicit (instruction.md:7). Seed checks: 'Fenwick'/'heads of terms' only in M-12; 'Probate' only in K-13; K-10 at 05-05T11:00:00Z exactly 7 days, K-11 one second later; K-17 held 3 May; K-2 held with version 'Landlords notice recieved.' - criteria match seed.

ONE INSTANCE grades an unrequired implementation structure: functional wall_added_live step 3 (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:86) says 'From Sian's session, replay Harriet's recorded wall request changed to lift Sian's own wall'. Only the add request has been recorded at that point (step 83 records the wall; the lift is first done in step 4, line 87). This presumes adding and lifting a wall are the same request with a toggled field - exactly the golden's shape (server.js:470-486, POST /api/matters/:id/walls with body {email, walled}; golden script functional.cjs:185 builds the lift by setting walled:false). Nothing public requires that shape; constraints prompt line 'Do not prescribe endpoint names or implementation structure', app_context 'Never guess routes', functional prompt 'Do not guess URL paths or API routes' and 'Any endpoint path, payload shape ... is acceptable' all forbid the judge from constructing a different lift route. Under 'A step you skipped ... or could not perform fails the criterion', a correct app fails this 2.0-weight binary criterion.

Lower-risk Notes (not counted as defects): polish transcript_print 'replies visibly indented under their parents' (polish/judge.toml:53) picks indentation as the thread cue; the brief only says 'in their threads' (walls-and-retention.md:35), though indentation is the professional default for a threaded document. Visual matter_sidebar 'the matter list beside the thread at desktop width' (visual/judge.toml:27) assumes a two-pane layout; a desktop chat sidebar is a professional default and the anchors grade clarity, so false-fail risk is small. polish phone_matter 'scrollWidth equals the viewport width' is the measurable form of 'without the page scrolling sideways' under Playwright's headless hidden scrollbars. message link 'following the link opens ... at that message' is implied by 'follow an old link' (walls-and-retention.md:17) and 'point at something said elsewhere'.

Evidence limits: source review plus the scripted golden index only; the golden passes step 3 because it uses the toggle shape, so golden runs cannot show the conforming-alternative failure. No configured judge run, Oracle or model score was measured or is claimed.
counterexample: A conforming app implements walls RESTfully: Harriet adds a wall with POST /api/matters/M-13/walls {email:'sian@...'} and lifts it with DELETE /api/matters/M-13/walls/sian@... . It refuses every Sian request on M-13 with a plain not-available, satisfying every public rule. In wall_added_live step 3 the judge has only the recorded POST; no field change turns it into a lift, and inventing the DELETE route is forbidden ('Never guess routes'). The step cannot be performed as written, so the judge fails the 2.0-weight criterion (or replays the add request, which proves nothing about lifting). Conversely a broken app that lets any walled staff member lift walls through a separate unrecorded route is never tested if the judge substitutes the add replay.
suggested_fix: Make step 3 independent of request shape: before walling Sian, have Harriet add and lift a wall for another staff member (e.g. Dev on M-13) with the app's controls, recording both requests, then wall Sian and from Sian's session replay the recorded lift request with Sian as the target; or replay the recorded wall request from Sian's session targeting another staff member (e.g. walling Dev from M-13) and require refusal - either way only a recorded request with a changed target/field is used.
